\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Invariance Truncation: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Lipschitz Boolean-to-Gaussian invariance bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_lipschitz_boolean_gaussian}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_lipschitz_boolean_gaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasInvarianceMoments_gaussianCoordinate, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasInvarianceMoments_standardGaussian, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasInvarianceMoments_uniformBoolCoordinate, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_uniformBool_pi_eq_expect, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_lipschitz, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval_fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.influence, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion}
\difficulty{5}
There exists a constant $K>0$ such that the following holds for all natural numbers
$n,d$, all functions $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ whose Walsh coefficients vanish on sets
of size greater than $d$, and all $\varepsilon\ge0$: if $\operatorname{Var}(f)\le1$ and
every coordinate influence satisfies $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\le\varepsilon$, then for every
$c\ge0$ and every $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
\[
\left|\mathbb E_{x\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^n)}\psi(f(x))-\mathbb
E_{z\sim\gamma^{\otimes n}}\psi\!\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\widehat f(S)\prod_{i\in
S}z_i\right)\right|\le Kc\,2^d\varepsilon^{1/4},
\]
where $\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian law on $\mathbb R$ and $\widehat f(S)$ are the
Walsh coefficients of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Degree bound for a low-degree truncation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lowDegreePart_polynomial_degree}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lowDegreePart_polynomial_degree}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,d\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. The Fourier coefficient family
of the degree-$d$ truncation of $f$ vanishes on every subset $S\subseteq[n]$ with
$|S|>d$; equivalently, that coefficient family has degree at most $d$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Variance of the low-degree Fourier truncation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lowDegreePart_variance_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.lowDegreePart_variance_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_eq_sum_nonempty_fourier, KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{4}
For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, every Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and every
degree cutoff $d\in\mathbb{N}$, the variance of the low-degree Fourier truncation of $f$
is at most the variance of $f$: $\operatorname{Var}(f^{\le d})\leq
\operatorname{Var}(f)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegative cutoff exponent]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_cutoff_nonneg}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_cutoff_nonneg}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every real $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1$,
\[
0\le \frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}{3}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential cutoff identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_cutoff_exp}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_cutoff_exp}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every real $\varepsilon>0$ and every real $\delta$,
\[
\exp\!\left(-\delta\,\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}{3}\right)=\varepsilon^{\delta/3}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cutoff power comparison]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_cutoff_power_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.invariance_cutoff_power_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For real numbers $\varepsilon,\delta$ with $0<\varepsilon\le1$ and $\delta\le1/20$,
\[
2^{\log(1/\varepsilon)/3}\,\varepsilon^{1/4}\le \varepsilon^{\delta/3}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[High-degree noise norm bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.highDegree_noise_l2Norm_le_exp}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.highDegree_noise_l2Norm_le_exp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_eq_sum_nonempty_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.parseval, KKL.fourierCoeff_highDegreePart, KKL.highDegreePart}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number and $f$ a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of
dimension $n$, with variance at most $1$. Let $0\le\delta\le1$ and $k\ge0$ be real
numbers. The $L^2$ norm of the part of the noise operator applied to $f$ with Fourier
degrees strictly greater than $\lfloor k\rfloor$ is at most $\exp(-\delta k)$.
\end{theorem}
